concept.subject: A star's blast spreading out in rings: a bright white shell around a small bright core, with orange filaments of the outer shock waves around it.
concept.composition: The bright shell is a wide oval in the middle of the picture, from a quarter to three quarters of the height and from a third to two thirds of the width, with the core star at its center a little above half height and a second bright star on its left rim. The orange outer shells spread around it out to a fifth and four fifths of the width and over nearly the full height; small stars dot the plain space beyond.
concept.layout: 34 round pegs and 127 bricks, the stage's last level with the original's split of 24 pegs and 90 bricks scaled. The inner shock ring is the rotating template's single wheel around the core: curved bricks broken into four slots, turning around a hub peg with four short spokes and a ring of pegs inside. A thin solid arc of the bright shell caps it under the cannon. Around it the shell and three shock waves are concentric rings of curved bricks broken into arcs and open at the top, and five rays of pegs run out through the gaps in them, a web of rings and spokes.

moving.what: the inner shock ring and its spokes

features: Last level of 24 pegs and 90 bricks (spec 8), scaled to 34 and 127

difficulty.note: Among the stage's hardest: with only 34 pegs most orange objects are bricks, the solid cap keeps straight shots off the turning core ring, and the shock rings stand between the cannon and the rays.

background.prompt: A nebula blown out into rings around a dying star in a soft lilac-gray outer space. A bright white and pale blue oval shell sits in the middle of the picture, from about a quarter to three quarters of the picture height and from about a third to two thirds of the width, with a small bright star at its center a little above half the height and a second bright star on its left rim. Around it, orange and dusty pink filaments of the outer shells spread out to about a fifth and four fifths of the width and over nearly the full height, fading toward the edges. Small stars dot the plain space beyond; the lower corners are plain.
